title: How Hunger Can Trigger Alcohol Cravings - Nautilus

text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementBiologyHow Hunger Can Trigger Alcohol CravingsAt least in fruit flies JCBy Jake Currie2:00 PM CDT on October 20, 2026Add Nautilus to Google“You’re not yourself when you’re hungry” isn’t just a memorable Snickers ad slogan, it also happens to be true. Our brains process information slightly differently depending on our internal state, whether we’re hungry, thirsty, in pain, etc. Of course, the same is true of other animals, even those with relatively simple brains like fruit flies. Now, a new study published in Current Biology finds that hunger may be involved with triggering cravings for alcohol (at least in the aforementioned fruit flies).Why study fruit flies to understand human brains? For starters, there’s a much broader toolkit available (including a map of the entire fly brain and a slew of genetic tools). It also helps to start with less complex neural circuitry. “If we can understand at a smaller level how an organism like a fly can remember alcohol, that is a step forward to understanding how humans associate cues with alcohol and can provide hints at how we can prevent relapse and treat addiction,” study author Lewis Sherer of Brown University explained in a statement.Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
